observations.details: Vercel preview protection prevented unauthenticated application-header inspection. No token or protection bypass was created. Redirect query parameters and cookies are deliberately omitted.

The application rendered its Protocol connections page on mainnet, with Zest and StackingDAO route choices, deposit/withdraw controls, and Connect to inspect your route. The notice stated: Vault release under review. New vault deposits are disabled. No wallet was connected.

Navigation rendered Your portfolio with the disconnected-wallet state: A wallet brings your positions into view. The page explained that connecting does not authorize any transaction. It did not display invented balances or position outcomes.
Both visited pages displayed the expected copper/charcoal interface and readable typography. No blank application page or visibly broken layout was observed in the desktop window.

The browser console recorded a CSP violation blocking https://vercel.live/_next-live/feedback/feedback.js under the application script-src policy. This is the Vercel preview feedback toolbar; the application pages remained functional. Existing injected wallet extensions also logged initialization conflicts, including competing provider-property definitions. These extension errors are not evidence that the reviewer connected or signed with a wallet. No Google-font CSP violation was visible in the inspected console. This review does not claim an error-free console.
observations.recommendation: Retain the restrictive application script policy unless preview feedback is an explicit requirement; do not broaden it solely to silence the optional toolbar warning.

fontAndDeploymentConfigurationReview.scope: Read-only review for the Vercel/Linux Node 24 deployment; no dependency installation or node_modules mutation during this review.
findings: The installer resolves the repository from its own file URL and checks all four required package manifests, lockfiles, and entrypoints before starting npm.
The static package list covers frontend, integrations/stacks, integrations/bitcoin, and integrations/pox5. Package and lockfile root dependency metadata agree.
The installer enforces Node 24, installs sequentially from lockfiles with lifecycle scripts disabled and development build dependencies included, then explicitly builds the Bitcoin package.
Process spawn errors, signals, and unsuccessful exit codes fail the installer. The inspected Bitcoin build uses TypeScript and has no prebuild or postbuild lifecycle script.
Vercel uses the workspace installer and frontend build command. Frontend package and lockfile engine metadata both specify Node 24.
The configured font-related CSP additions are limited to https://fonts.googleapis.com in style-src and https://fonts.gstatic.com in font-src.
limits: Successful build and install results were provided by the implementation agent; this reviewer did not rerun dependency installation.

Actual authenticated response headers and successful Google-font network responses were not independently captured. Visual rendering and the source CSP configuration do not substitute for that network evidence.

relatedLocalReview.details: Earlier independent local review covered seven views at 1440px, 768px and 375px, keyboard navigation, consent controls, RPC failure handling, public read-only balances, and native funding gates. Those local results are not represented as hosted mobile or hosted integration results.

releaseLimits: This bounded smoke review confirms rendering of two authenticated preview routes and the observed vault deposit release gate. It does not certify production safety, wallet transaction completion, every direct-protocol gate, or approval to enable funding.
